title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## Effector‑Centric NMPC for Tiltable Quadrotors

### The Breakthrough
The authors present a four‑rotor tiltable multirotor equipped with an onboard nonlinear model predictive controller running at 100 Hz. A dual disturbance‑rejection strategy enables offset‑free omnidirectional aerial manipulation, demonstrated with a 90° cartwheel, whiteboard pushing, and continuous 360° valve turning.

### The Caveats
The paper provides no quantitative comparison to existing controllers, making it unclear whether the claimed performance exceeds prior methods.

## Jetson‑ORB‑SLAM3 Edge GPU Port

### The Breakthrough
ORB‑SLAM3 is ported to the NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano GPU, reproducing 94.7 % of keypoints and 99.9 % of descriptor bits while achieving sub‑centimeter trajectory error on standard benchmarks and sustaining 32 FPS with a 180× faster FP16 TensorRT loop‑closure engine.

### The Caveats
Evaluation is limited to static benchmark datasets; no real‑world robot or dynamic‑scene tests are presented.

## Unitree ‘Superman’ Humanoid IPO

### The Breakthrough
Unitree unveiled a “Superman” humanoid that can hop 2 m high and run at 12.66 m/s, showcasing advances in bipedal actuation, and announced a partnership with Nvidia to develop embodied AI models.

### The Caveats
Performance figures are product specifications without independent benchmarking or deployment data.

## 1872 Robotic Steel‑Fabrication Factory

### The Breakthrough
The startup integrates AI‑driven software with industrial robots to automate most steps of steel skid fabrication, targeting roughly 80 % autonomy and a prototype slated for 2027 to serve data‑center and modular nuclear markets.

### The Caveats
The claim rests on a company announcement; no independent performance data or real‑world trials are provided.

## Hydra‑0 Action‑Flow World Model

### The Breakthrough
Hydra‑0 treats robot actions as pixel motion, cutting robot‑motion error by 90.4 % and object‑motion error by 60.2 % versus a baseline, achieving r = 0.96 correlation on the RoboLab benchmark and learning an inverse mode that maps human‑demonstrated object flow to executable robot motions without task‑specific data.

### The Caveats
Results are confined to a simulated benchmark and have never been validated on physical robots.

## Foxglove Agentic Workflows

### The Breakthrough
Foxglove adds an LLM‑driven sidebar agent and MCP server that automatically selects tools such as FoxQL and MCAP diagnosis, exposing an API to external agents like Claude and Claude, with an evaluation pipeline for prompt and tool changes.

### The Caveats
No performance metrics, user study, or hardware validation are supplied.

## PRISM Multimodal Manipulation Dataset

### The Breakthrough
PRISM offers over 5 000 teleoperated trajectories across 25 precision, contact‑rich industrial tasks, capturing synchronized multi‑view RGB‑D, force/torque, tactile, and robot‑state data for a total of 45 hours.

### The Caveats
The release lacks benchmarks, baseline comparisons, or real‑robot evaluations, leaving its practical impact uncertain.

## FCC Ban on Foreign‑Made Robots

### The Breakthrough
The FCC adds “advanced robotic devices” to its Covered List, requiring new sales in the U.S. to contain at least 65 % domestic component value (rising to 75 % by 2029) for devices such as humanoids, quadrupeds, vacuums, and lawn mowers.

### The Caveats
The article provides no empirical analysis of cost or supply‑chain feasibility, so the rule’s effects remain unsubstantiated.

### Priority
The tiltable‑multirotor NMPC demo showcases a concrete, hardware‑level advance in aerial manipulation that directly impacts embodied AI research today.

### One action
Monitor the authors’ code repository or upcoming video demos to see the controller in action and assess its applicability to your own aerial‑robot projects.

### What to watch
Several items explore new control and perception pipelines: the tiltable‑multirotor NMPC, the Jetson‑accelerated ORB‑SLAM3, and Hydra‑0’s pixel‑flow world model each push toward more capable real‑world robots, while PRISM provides data that could benchmark future algorithms.
